description:
Think you’re all set for college with just your laptop? Not so fast! As any computer user knows, you need a few accessories to fully unlock the potential of any laptop, whether to make it more useful, more efficient, or just more comfortable for all-day sessions.

If you’re going to be spending a lot of time on that laptop—or if you’re a parent and your kid is the one heading off to college—then it’s a good idea to make sure it’s well-equipped to be used to its fullest.

We’ve curated the most essential laptop add-ons that won’t break the bank, with each one below the $100 mark (and some of them way below that mark). Mix and match what you (or your child) will need for the upcoming year with these ultimate value laptop accessories.
title: 9 laptop accessories every college student needs, all under $100

description:
Laptops are great if you need portability, but they’re also expensive. You’re paying for a lot of hardware that may not matter if your computer never leaves your desk. Since laptops cram all of their components into a single device, they’re much more expensive to manufacture and ship, especially in today’s economy.

That’s where mini PCs shine. These tiny desktops pack surprisingly powerful hardware into a box that can fit in the palm of your hand, yet they often cost a fraction of the price of a similarly powerful laptop. That means more of your money goes toward the processor, memory, and storage instead of the built-in screen and battery. 

The tradeoff, of course, is that you’ll need to supply your own monitor, keyboard, and mouse. But if you already have those sitting on your desk—or you’re replacing an aging desktop—that’s hardly a d
title: These 5 mini PCs make laptops look wildly overpriced

description:
How much is your face worth to you? This week, Google announced you can start using it as a form of authentication—a way to get into your account.

Here’s how it works: You take a “video selfie” of yourself and upload to Google’s servers. It’s kept on file for reference. In the future, if you want to log in or recover your account, you take a new video selfie and Google compares the two. If its algorithms believe they’re a match, you get into your account.

Welcome to Safe Mode, your weekly report for pressing security and privacy news—and what steps to take next. Want this newsletter to come directly to your inbox? Si
title: Google wants your face to be your backup password. I’d wait

description:
If you regularly move files between your phone, tablet, and computer, you’ve probably run into the same annoyance I have. AirDrop works great (I love it!), but not all of my devices are Apple devices. That’s when I turned to LocalSend.

LocalSend is a free, open-source app that lets you send files between devices on the same Wi-Fi network, no matter what operating system they use. Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iPhone all work together without any extra setup. Like AirDrop, but for everything.

It’s dead simple to use, too. Install the app on your devices, make sure they’re connected to the same local network, and nearby devices will appear automatically. Select the files you want to send, choose the destination device, and you’re done. Photos, videos, documents, folders, and other files transfer d
title: The free file-sharing app I install on every new device
